speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The MCA allows for Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPAs) to be registered with the Public Guardian.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The LPA is a legal instrument through which a person, called a "donor", appoints one or more persons, called "donees", to make decisions on the donor’s personal welfare and/or property and affairs, should the donor lose mental capacity in the future to make such decisions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The MCA also allows the Court to appoint a person, called "deputy", to make certain decisions on behalf of a person who lacks mental capacity but has not made an LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The key difference between a donee and a deputy is that a donee is appointed by the donor when he or she has mental capacity, while a deputy is appointed by the Court after the person has lost mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The pandemic has shown that life can be unpredictable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We never know when events that could result in the loss of mental capacity, such as accidents and diseases, may strike.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Making our LPAs early offers peace of mind for ourselves and our family.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, Mr Low Kim Leng, a 69-year-old retiree, and his wife made their LPAs after witnessing how the LPA ensured that the affairs of their relatives with dementia were well taken care of.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mr Francis Ng, a 60-year-old semi-retiree, also attested to the importance of making an LPA early as this would help his family avoid the stress and costs of applying to the Court for a deputyship order.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: He shared that because his father had not made an LPA before losing mental capacity, he was unable to manage his father’s Housing and Development Board (HDB) property on his behalf.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Instead, he had to apply to the Court to be appointed as a deputy and reflected that the process was very stressful as it was long and tedious, in addition to having to care for his father.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Unfortunately, his father passed away before the deputyship application was granted.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Now, he urges his peers to make their LPAs as soon as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This means Singaporeans need not pay any application fee when making their LPAs during this period.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They will need to pay for the LPA Certification service, which is about $50 or less, based on rates charged by those found on a list of the top 10 most visited doctors who are serving as Certificate Issuers as at January this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: LPA Form 1 is the standard LPA form used by 98% of donors to confer on their donees the power to make decisions on the personal welfare and/or property and affairs of the donor.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The remaining 2% use LPA Form 2, which require lawyers to draw up the specific and customised powers to be granted by the donor.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In preparing for this Bill, we have sought feedback from the legal and medical sectors, as well as members of the public.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They have provided valuable insights and they are supportive of the amendments we are proposing.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: New subsections (5) to (14) of section 11, which are inserted by clause 4 of the Bill, will allow us to recognise an electronic copy of an LPA registered prior to the launch of OPGO to be free from error and to be treated as the lasting power of attorney, if certain conditions are met.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Other transactions such as the filing of a Deputy Report with the Office of the Public Guardian will be lodged via OPGO as well.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is in line with the Government’s commitment to harness technology to better serve Singaporeans and so that all donors and donees can reap the benefits of going digital.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will support those who are less tech savvy so that the gains will be enjoyed by everyone.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: LPAs today are made and executed in hard copy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, Dr Sin Yong, a Certificate Issuer who certifies that a donor has mental capacity to make an LPA, shared that doing away with hard copies could reduce the hassle of passing around paper forms.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Indeed, by enabling LPAs to be made online, there will be greater convenience, efficiency and security for our citizens.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: First, donees will be able to accept their appointments more conveniently.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Donees will not need to append their wet-ink signatures before a witness or to affix physical seals on the LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Instead, donees will be notified of the donor’s intention to appoint them via SMS and email.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They can then log on to OPGO via Singpass to accept the appointment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is especially beneficial if donees are overseas and unable to return to Singapore to do so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will also legally recognise electronically signed LPAs as deeds.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, hard copy LPAs must have wet-ink signatures appended and seals affixed by the donors to be executed as deeds.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Going forward, the donor will sign the LPA using his National Digital Identity in OPGO in the presence of a Certificate Issuer, instead of appending wet-ink signatures and affixing seals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Certificate Issuers can be accredited medical practitioners, practising lawyers and registered psychiatrists.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The new section 12A of the Act inserted by clause 6 of the Bill sets out the requirements for the LPA to be executed electronically as a deed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Second, digitalisation will cut the time taken to complete and register an LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A handful of cases may require manual processing, that will take about eight working days.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This three-week window starts from the date the Public Guardian notifies the donee or donees of the acceptance of the donor’s application to register the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If there are no objections at the end of this three-week waiting period, the Public Guardian will register the LPA instrument.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: On a related note, we will also tap on Singpass to retrieve personal information via MyInfo.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This auto-populates the donor’s particulars into the online LPA, thus increasing the ease of making an LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Third, robust measures ensure that the LPA is properly made by the donor and not by an impersonator.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In this regard, we have retained the critical requirement for the donor to execute the LPA before a Certificate Issuer.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under paragraph 2(1)(e) of the First Schedule to the Act, the Certificate Issuer will need to certify that the donor understands the purpose of the LPA and the scope of the authority conferred under it, and the donor is not under undue pressure or duress to make the LPA and that there is nothing else which would prevent the LPA from being created.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Certificate Issuer must be satisfied that these conditions are fulfilled before the Certificate Issuer may certify the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Both the donor and Certificate Issuer will sign using a secure electronic signature, which is enabled by the National Digital Identity, before submitting it online for processing.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Electronic LPAs that are easily retrievable will also reduce the risk of damaging or misplacing hard copy LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Donors and donees will be able to easily access the registered LPA in OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: When transacting with third parties on behalf of the donor, donees may request for the Office of the Public Guardian to send an electronic copy of the LPA to the third party.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This assures third parties that the LPA is indeed the true and latest version.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Additionally, individuals will be able to conduct online LPA searches and, subject to approval, request for certified true copies of the registered LPAs via OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Filing deputyship reports will also be made easier via OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, deputies can use an online finance tracker to manage the incapacitated person's income and expenses.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Certain fields in the reports will also be prefilled with information from court documents, the previous year's report and the finance tracker.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Deputies will not have to manually complete their reports or compile their supporting documents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Instead, they can focus on caring for their incapacitated loved ones.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We want all donors and donees to benefit from digitalisation and this includes those who have registered their LPAs before the launch of OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Office of the Public Guardian will make available electronic copies of all existing LPAs on OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The risk of error in transferring these existing LPAs onto OPGO is low as there is neither extraction nor entry of new data.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nevertheless, we will send a notice to all existing donors and donees via registered post, requiring them to verify the accuracy of the electronic copy on OPGO against their registered LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If the donor has lost mental capacity, any donee may notify the Public Guardian on his, or her behalf.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If there is a notification of error within the 90-day period, the electronic copy will be treated as the LPA on the 91st day, or the day on which the Public Guardian rectifies the error, whichever is later.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is to allow donors and donees to fully benefit from having the entire 90-day period to notify the Public Guardian of any error.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is provided for under the new section 15A of the Act which is inserted by clause 9 of the Bill.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nevertheless, I strongly encourage all donees and donors to make the necessary verifications within the 90-day period.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under paragraphs 7(4), 17, 18, 19 and 20 of the amended First Schedule substituted by clause 17 of the Bill, the Public Guardian is required to attach a note to an LPA on the occurrence of certain events.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Such events include the bankruptcy of the donee, which terminates the donee's authority in relation to property and affairs, and the donee's loss of mental capacity, which terminates the donee's appointment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: All such notes will be attached to the electronic copy of the LPA in OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As such, the electronic copy of the LPA in OPGO will be the most up-to-date copy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Third parties transacting with donees should ask for the electronic copy when verifying the donee's authority.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Office of the Public Guardian will send the electronic copy to the third party through OPGO and upon the donee's request.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: There had been concerns about the exploitative behaviour of donees in past discussions of the Mental Capacity Act.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Such cases form a very small minority and we had amended the Mental Capacity Act in 2016 to put in place pre-emptive actions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, the Court may under the existing section 36A(3) of the Act, suspend the donee, or deputy's powers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If he or she has engaged in conduct affecting his or her suitability to be a donee or deputy and there is a risk of dissipation of the incapacitated persons assets.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: But we can do more to protect the donors proactively even before an LPA is registered.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: There may be rare instances where a person attempts to unduly influence many donors to appoint him or her as their donee.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The donee may stand to gain if any or all of the donors lose their capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Some donees may also fail to disclose their multiple appointments to donors who might take that into consideration.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Only the number of LPAs for which the prospective donee has already been appointed or intends to be appointed may be disclosed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: No other confidential information such as the names of the other donors will be given.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, this alone should suffice for the donor to pause and reconsider the choice of his or her donee.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I am mindful that some of us may be less comfortable navigating online services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will provide support and work with our community partners to ensure that assistance is readily available.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is promising as it indicates that family support is strong with many donees often helping their older relatives to fill up the hard copy LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As we roll out OPGO later this year, I am confident that many Singaporeans will continue to rely on their family to assist with their LPA applications online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To facilitate this, we have designed OPGO to leverage the multi-user SMS two-factor authentication, or 2FA service provided by Singpass.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Elderly users who do not know how to log on to OPGO via Singpass may opt for the SMS one-time PIN, or OTP, to be sent to the child's mobile phone number.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The child would then be able to help the elderly log on to OPGO via Singpass.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will make OPGO as user-friendly as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Videos and resource guides will be incorporated into the system to guide users in the completion of their LPAs online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This includes text-to-speech functions for the visually impaired.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The online guides, videos and instructions will also be made available in vernacular languages.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Members of the public who need help may also set up an appointment for one-on-one consultation at the Office of the Public Guardian.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will work closely with our partners to ensure that help is accessible at various community touchpoints.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Individuals may approach their nearest Citizen Connect Centre located at selected Community Centres or the Public Service Centre, or PSC, at Our Tampines Hub.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We also welcome other community partners to work with us to bring more on board as we begin this digitalisation journey.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Electronic submissions of LPA applications will be the norm to ensure that the public reaps the full benefits of digitalisation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: But there may be exceptional circumstances that warrant the use of a hard copy form which are specified in the new section 10C(2) of the Act inserted by clause 3 of the Bill.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, where personal circumstances or physical disability of the donor and/or donee results in their inability to make or sign the instrument using OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Other instances include cases where the donor or donee is ineligible for a Singpass account if he or she is not a Singapore Citizen, Permanent Resident or long-term resident.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will also allow hard copies submissions if there is a severe and prolonged system outage.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This includes the very real risk that we may one day lose our mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is wise to pre-plan and have peace of mind knowing that we have entrusted our well-being to a person who will act in our best interests should the need arise.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Making our LPAs early will also make the caregiving journey less stressful for our loved ones, who will be spared the stressful and costly process of obtaining a Court order to be appointed as deputy.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It is certainly a useful legal instrument that was introduced in 2010.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But the number of persons who have made it is not high.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This low number could be due to a number of reasons.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: One often incited is a stigma about speaking about death.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Understandably, we might not be comfortable discussing the possibility that we will be unable to make decisions for ourselves.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Talking about end of life matters is still seen as a taboo or inauspicious for some.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We say we will do it, but most of us will procrastinate and end up not doing it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: These are important matters, whether it is making a will or LPA, but we do not pay enough attention to it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Some years ago, my wife and I finally accompanied each other and we did both.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Since then, I could say so to a lot of people, with stronger conviction, whether it is to friends or residents, why they should do it and do it now, not tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We do this certainly not for our sake, but for the people that matter to us – our family and loved ones.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In the long term, with an ageing population, these conversations will increase in frequency whether in public forums or private spaces.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As unpleasant as the possibility may be, in the event that someone can no longer make their own decisions, an LPA empowers their close relatives to act on their behalf, for elderly individuals or couples without family support, the Professional Deputies and Donee Scheme provides a source of potential donors for an LPA.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Another reason for the low numbers might be a lack of public awareness.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: MSF has been promoting LPA through Community Centres, Senior Activity Centres and radio channels.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: However, members of the public might be unfamiliar with what an LPA entails or are confused by the decisions needed: what powers to grant donees whether multiple donees should act jointly or separately, and so on?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For this, we will need to step up our outreach and publicity efforts.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Although events and roadshows are good idea, awareness tends to fade if they are not sustained over time.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Furthermore, the effectiveness of in-person events may be limited by evolving safe distancing measures.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Last, I think perhaps the most likely is just a lack of attention.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Our bias is to ignore the long term or to shy away from thinking about difficult topics.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This cannot be fixed by more public dialogues or information and education.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It requires each of us to decide for ourselves that we need to be responsible and aware of our own mortality and to prepare for it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: LPA is certainly a useful instrument which deserves to be better known and more widely used.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At the same time, even as we promote its use, we should see its limitations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Under the MCA, a donor can confer on the donee the authority to make decisions regarding the donor's welfare, property and affairs if the donor becomes unable to make these decisions themselves.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For most of us, we will find making LPAs digitally much easier and more convenient.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The use of Singpass also means that the user's details are automatically entered, making it more convenient for LPA to be made while not compromising on data security.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: However, I do have the following concerns on the proposed amendments to the Act.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We need to ensure that those who are less tech savvy are not left behind.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As mentioned earlier, the elderly are a prime target audience for LPA to be made.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Yet, many of them may be unfamiliar with the tools or even terminology that is used.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For example, they may not know how to navigate the Singpass app or website with the two-factor authentication.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: While Singpass now allows users to sign into family members' accounts, not all elderly have family members on hand to help them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Yes, MSF will assist those who have difficulty navigating the OPGO system by making Internet-enabled devices and trained staff available at community centres (CCs).

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This ensures that people do not have to venture beyond their neighbourhoods, making the process quick and easy.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: However, not all CCs will have these facilities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For those who need help, travelling further to an unfamiliar place may greatly discourage them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In fact, I know it does, especially for the elderly.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If help was available at all CCs, I am quite sure it would lead to a greater take-up rate.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Yes, I recognise that more resources will be required but I believe it will be monies well spent.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Still, even with various forms of assistance and accessibility measures, the five steps of the OPGO process may be hard to track, with multiple notifications and confirmations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For this, giving donors a physical checklist of the steps involved and the stage they are at – similar to reminders on vaccination cards – may be useful.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Besides improving accessibility, with more services and applications transitioning online, we also need to watch out for scams, which are getting increasingly sophisticated.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For now, there are safeguards in place such as Singpass users being prompted to verify the authenticity of websites before logging on.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: However, scams are getting more complicated, with fake websites resembling other Government agencies' websites being reported.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We must keep our guard up and prevent such scams.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Some elderly individuals or those who are less tech-savvy might request friends or family members to help them with their submissions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I think this is quite normal in the course of business.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: While the majority of such cases will be safe, there could be those who abuse their trust and appoint themselves as donee.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The security and sanctity of the LPA are worth the increase in administrative work, in my opinion.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This safeguard, I feel, can be made stronger.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We should not subject the Public Guardian to such a heavy responsibility.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Public Guardian should not really have to exercise judgement about when to step in.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: With the disclosure, the donor can then decide if he or she wants to continue making the LPA with this donee.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In the long run, as we improve access and strengthen safeguards against abuse of the process, hopefully more people will make an LPA.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Notwithstanding these suggestions, I support the proposed amendments.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Another group of persons who would benefit are court-appointed deputies who will also be able to transact online with the OPG and retrieve information more easily.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There are also provisions to alert donors of suspicious circumstances surrounding the intended LPAs, which are well-intentioned.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: While some have called for this requirement to be done away and to allow donors to appear remotely, I disagree.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The in-person appearance is important as it will enable the Certificate Issuer – whether a lawyer, a psychiatrist or a credited medical practitioner – to make some assessment as to whether the donor is making the document out of free will.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In comparison, having the donor appear online may be convenient.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But online certification also carries a higher risk that there are unseen persons or forces adding pressure to the donor to execute the document.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Similarly, out of caution, the Government has decided not to expand the category of professions who can issue LPAs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We have already seen hostile litigation among family members over LPAs, with lawyers and doctors dragged in to justify their assessments of whether the donor was mentally capable or incapable at various points in time.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is prudent not to include other suggested groups like religious and grassroots leaders without much more consideration.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As with all things digital, there are concerns about those who would find it difficult or even oppressive to do so and how we would need to include them in the implementation of the OPG online.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Member of Parliament for Sengkang GRC, Mr Louis Chua, will elaborate on this while my colleague in Aljunied GRC, Mr Leon Perera, will offer his suggestions for some reforms for the future.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For my part, I wish to seek clarifications about three clauses in the Bill: the proposed section 10(C)(2), clause 12 and clause 17(2).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This will allow the Public Guardian to provide alternative ways to transact with its office if the transaction cannot be carried out through the online system and "due to a person's physical disability or other circumstance or because the system is unavailable or for any other reason." It would be useful for the Ministry to elaborate on the scope of these exceptions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: When we say a person is unable to use the system due to physical disability, are we referring to a person who cannot use his fingers to key in a digital identification or who is visually impaired?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What is the scope of the wide phrase "for any other reason"?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Would this include, for instance, persons who are hospitalised or incarcerated?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Second, clause 12 will give new powers to the Public Guardian to interview the donor.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is further stated that one of the grounds for such suspicion is the number of LPAs registered or pending registration with the same donee.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Although it is stated that the Public Guardian can require the donor to be interviewed, it is not stated what the consequence will be if the donor does not attend.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This could happen for innocent reasons like not being physically mobile.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What will the Public Guardian do in that circumstance?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, the Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that the Public Guardian might apply to Court for a decision on whether the LPA should be deregistered.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could he clarify, for example, whether the Public Guardian might even decline to register the LPA in the first instance?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Next, on what basis would the Public Guardian find reasonable cause to suspect fraud or undue pressure?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Will the Public Guardian largely rely on information given to it rather than initiate its own investigations?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For example, if I am named a donee by three family members, will that be considered suspicious?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, the likelihood of family members appointing the same donee is increasing as many of us need to assist elderly relatives who are unmarried or childless.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This may be allowed with prior approval if the Public Guardian is satisfied that there is "good reason" why the donor cannot appear physically before a Certificate Issuer to execute the electronic document.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Given what we have discussed about the risk of not appearing in person before the Certificate Issuer, it will be useful to know what scenarios are being contemplated as constituting good reasons.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, the Ministry has stated in its public consultation summary that exceptional circumstances will need to be shown.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could the Parliamentary Secretary elaborate on these circumstances?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For example, does it include situations where donors are overseas for long periods of time?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I support the proposed amendments to the Mental Capacity Act.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: New safeguards to check on donees and cybersecurity features are also added.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These changes bode well for Singaporeans who were previously deterred by the longer and more cumbersome process and especially for those who are IT-savvy and who can self-help.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, I would like to highlight four concerns which I hope the Ministry can address.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Concern number one: the underlying inertia of Singaporeans in making an LPA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Despite the encouraging increase in the number of LPAs registered – more than 20,000 annually in recent years – the total number remains relatively low compared to the population which is eligible.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: More than one million Singaporeans are above the age of 55.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: More Singaporeans are expected to be hit by dementia or loss of mental capacity gradually.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In 2018, ChannelNewsAsia ran an article featuring more Singaporeans being diagnosed with dementia at an even younger age and even younger age.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is clearly an increasing number of Singaporeans at risk of losing their mental capacity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is also an inertia to take the initiative by many to apply for an LPA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, even if the expected number of LPAs is expected to rise to more than 30,000 with the proposed amendments, there is still a large pool of Singaporeans who need more than a nudge.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A more aggressive and robust communications and outreach plan is in need.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The current video example available to MSF and the other measures are obviously not enough.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I strongly advise the development and implementation of a comprehensive communications and outreach plan covering: (a) different target audiences with demographics and so forth; (b) analyses of their communications style, the language, channels of communication; (c) ways by which they can be reached through an effective marketing mix or communications mix of TV, radio, print, grassroots workshops, volunteer workshops and incentive programmes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Concern number two: the vulnerable and the need to include and protect their interests.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They may be the less educated, not defined by one’s paper qualifications, who may not understand the concept or need for an LPA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They may be the less technically savvy who are averse to the use of Singpass, electronic signatures and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Then, there are persons with disabilities who are differently abled and they are different.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some may have mental capacity but will still need help to understand and complete the process of LPA application and registration.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some may not pass the test for full mental capacity as stated in MCA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, that is to understand, to be able to retain information, to weigh decision and to communicate.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They and/or their caregivers will need advice and guidance on whether LPAs are relevant or whether deputies should be appointed to protect them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is an obvious need to seriously invest in a track for the vulnerable.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I suggest that the Ministry considers the following options to ensure that the vulnerable are included and protected.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One, to set up specific LPA clinics at the major community centres staffed by trained professionals with technical knowledge and/or language fluency that is required.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Much like the vaccination centres albeit at a smaller scale.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These can be permanent for bigger towns for longer period or they can be mobile LPA clinics to serve smaller precincts.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And second is to consider adopting a parallel run allowing for a co-existing physical and online system until our nation is more ready to go fully online in this matter.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One important party to the process of LPA application is the Certificate Issuer or CI.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The CI is a witness for the donor and certifies that the donor has the capacity to make an LPA and that there is no fraud or undue influence used to induce the donor to make the LPA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The current Act states that the LPA CI must be either one, a medical practitioner accredited by the Public Guardian; or a practicing lawyer; or a registered psychiatrist.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Findings in countries such as Hong Kong, for instance, have shown that many do not approach these professionals for various reasons: the cost or the perception of the cost; and the fear or discomfort of approaching or interacting with these experts.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, the professional pool is larger than that in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Whilst technical qualification is a proxy of a CI’s competency, it is only one of several competencies required of a good CI.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A responsible CI should be able to and is interested in detecting the donors who are vulnerable, unduly pressured or influenced into giving power to certain donees.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Why can they not be included in the pool of CIs, so that the pool can be enlarged for choice by the donor?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I recommend that the pool of CIs be enlarged.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Concern four and the final concern: families of persons who lack or lost mental capacity and are without LPA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They and their families who have to decide on their behalf and look after them are often clueless and helpless.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Usually, it is too late by the time they know about this and the process often takes too long, leaving the family in limbo and distress.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While progress have been made to encourage deputyships for clients in disability organisations – I know such as MINDS for the intellectually disabled – there is still a sizeable population out there who need to know about the matters of deputyship appointments.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In summary, Sir, the proposed amendments provide for welcomed changes to an otherwise more cumbersome system.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have listed four major concerns and provided recommendations for the Ministry’s consideration.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Resources will be needed but they will be monies and time well invested.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The cost of not investing in this important life planning tool will most certainly be higher later.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My party Chair Ms Sylvia Lim has spoken in support of the Bill and has posed important clarifying questions and suggestions, as will my Parliamentary colleague Mr Louis Chua.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I shall limit my speech to a few technical suggestions for future consideration.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Some donors may not necessarily have physical disabilities but may be uncomfortable with the prospect of transacting purely online over such an important legal act.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This phenomenon may have been elevated by the publicity surrounding Internet frauds and personal data being compromised through various data breaches.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: MSF says it will reach out to users in need through the Citizen Connect Centres at community centres and the Integrated Public Service Centre at Tampines Hub.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Some jurisdictions require proactive regular reports from donees or guardians, particularly those with financial responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In Victoria state in Australia, for example, administrators must submit financial statements to the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal on an annual basis and otherwise as directed The New York Mental Hygiene Law requires guardians to report on their activities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The guardian must file an initial report no later than 90 days after being appointed by the Court.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In the initial report, the guardian who has been granted powers with respect to property management must document a complete inventory of properties and financial resources of the "incapable" person.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For personal needs, the guardian must provide a plan of care.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The definition for what constitutes such major decisions could be clearly spelt out in the legislation or subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such a requirement would provide the OPG with more information on how powers are being exercised under the Act, which would be useful for subsequent policy reviews.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such a requirement may also make the donees take the exercise of their responsibilities a little more seriously when it comes to making very major decisions on behalf of their donors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I would stress that I am not suggesting that donees be made to file detailed descriptions of every single decision they make on behalf of the donor, or annual reports and so on and so forth, as this is too onerous.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Substituted decision-making enables a proxy to make decisions on behalf of another person who is incapable; therefore, the concerned individual has no right to make a decision for himself or herself unless the substitutive decision-making framework is reversed or mitigated through some form of legal action.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: One counter-argument to any move towards a supported decision-making model may be that the substitutive decision-making model may not be as paternalistic as it sounds right now.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In the words of Assoc Prof Chin Jing Ji in an article in the journal of the College of Family Physicians, and I quote, “section 6 of the MCA defines best interests to include reasonably ascertainable past and present wishes and feelings, beliefs and values of the person, and other factors of significance.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, the MCA insists that before an act is done, or a decision is made, due consideration must be made to achieve the intended purpose in a way that is less restrictive on the person’s rights and freedom of action.” But, Sir, at best, the MCA is ambiguous as to whether it wants primarily to advocate autonomy or beneficence for the person lacking mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This ambiguity could allow for some interpretation in favour of supported decision-making at the practical level, but may also make decision-making challenging for the donee, potentially leading them to err on the side of caution, meaning to err on the side of paternalism.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It is known within the medical community that the best interests of patients can sometimes come into conflict with substitute decision-making.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Clinicians may be left in a difficult position when best interest standards are in conflict with each other.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Some argue that the role that the managing physician plays in consensus-building is a potential solution.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This problem is further complicated by the presence of paid professionals in the LPA system.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Professional donees with little knowledge, no more than the doctor, about the donor’s preferences might be more likely to employ a standardised, paternalistic approach towards decision-making on behalf of the donor.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In the supported decision-making paradigm, the individual receives support from a trusted individual, a network of individuals or entities to make personal, financial and legal decisions that must be followed by a third party such as financial institutions, business, health professionals and service providers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Depending on the needs of the individual with a disability, depending on their particular condition, the supported person will aid the individual to understand the relevant issues and information and make decisions based on her own preferences.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: If necessary, the person providing support interprets and communicates the individual's preferences and desires to third parties, so that they can be realised.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Another example of a supported decision-making model is the Swedish "legal mentor" who acts as the individual's agent, with the individual's consent.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Supported decision-making recognises that even people who have difficulty making choices, formulating decisions and communicating their preferences can make positive choices.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The CRPD Committee has repeatedly called for the replacement of substitutive decision-making systems with supported decision-making systems.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Moving in this direction may better promote and protect the rights of persons who require support in exercising their legal capacity in line with what they believe to be the mental capacity, the degree of mental capacity that they have.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Death and taxes are both as unwelcome, yet both are an essential part of our lives.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We have to think, plan and eventually execute the provisions for our mortality.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I see this as an important first step that will provide Singaporeans and their families with better support in dealing with life’s vicissitudes pertaining to loss of mental capacity, terminal illness, end of life and distribution of assets to loved ones post-life.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I made the call for digitalisation of LPAs and Wills on 7 April 2020 in this House when we were debating the COVID-19 (Temporary Provisions) Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I had also made calls to modernise and simplify the probate processes for several years now.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I do hope that in the near future lay persons will be able to access digital platforms to make not only LPAs but digital wills, advance medical directives and applications for Grants of Probate or Letters of Administration for straightforward probate matters without fuss, with little costs and from the comfort of their homes.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: At the same time, I do recognise that we still have a digital divide in our community and hon Member Ms Denise Phua spoke cogently about this point, drawing from surveys done by IMDA.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I, therefore, would like to join her and hon Member of Parliament Mr Seah Kian Peng in their call to provide tangible support to persons who are not digitally savvy.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: A number of hon Members of Parliament who spoke before me also dealt with this provision including hon Member Ms Sylvia Lim.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I applaud the move to enlarge the Public Guardian’s responsibilities so as to better protect the donor’s interests at the outset before an LPA is made.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I do not see this as an extension of duties; the PG taking over the responsibility of ensuring that the donee is a suitable person.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: That responsibility must sit squarely with the donor.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, I think it is good that the PG provides the necessary support to the donor in terms of giving relevant information and putting the donor on notice before he makes the important decision on the choice of his donee.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For example, it may serve the donor’s interest if the PG shares with the donor information as to whether the proposed donee has any criminal convictions dealing with theft, cheating, extortion, criminal breach of trust or an offence involving fraud or dishonesty.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Such information is not easily accessible by members of public, even though these are matters of public record since convictions are almost always pronounced in open Court.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Currently, the Court already has the power to revoke the LPA or direct that the LPA not to be registered on this ground if the conviction post-dates his appointment as donee.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The presumption here, I gather, is that the donor would know or act with reasonable diligence to establish the proposed donee’s background beforehand.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But, in practice, this is not necessarily the case.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Before I sit down, I would like to take this opportunity to join the hon Parliamentary Secretary in his clarion call to fellow Singaporeans who have not done so to make LPAs so that they can minimise the trouble to their loved ones who have to bear the responsibility of caring for them should they lose their mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Each one of these instruments play an important role in estate planning and helps provide peace of mind for our loved ones should something untoward happen in our lives.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While we are still fortunate to be in good health and of sound mental capacity today, an LPA arguably also provides us with the serenity of knowing full well, that there will be someone we trust to undertake key decisions for us, should we lose mental capacity one day.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Beyond the technical amendments to this Bill, the key question I have for the Ministry is thus, do we have a target to aspire to, in terms of the timeline, the number and percentage of LPA registrations in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Beyond the digitalisation of the LPAs and the waiver of the application fee for Form 1 since September 2014, what more is being done, and how much resources are being dedicated to ensuring that we raise the awareness of LPAs and, ultimately, the number of LPA registrations in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Looking into the details of the Bill, my first clarification is on section 31A, which my colleague Ms Sylvia Lim has discussed.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While the new section allows for the Public Guardian to interview donors if there is reasonable cause to suspect that fraud or undue pressure was used to induce the donor to execute the LPA or to appoint a particular donee, I wonder if a caveat mechanism can be put in place as a preventive measure to protect vulnerable persons and prevent abuse, rather than just a risk-based approach of requiring an interview when risks are identified?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This could involve, for example, having a next-of-kin or appointed caregiver submitting a declaration, substantiated with medical opinion that a person already lacks mental capacity or have intellectual disabilities, and that any attempts by the person to register for an LPA would raise an immediate red flag.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: My main concern, however, is that surrounding the transition to a purely electronic transaction system, the Office of the Public Guardian Online electronic system (OPGO).

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I consider myself a digital native and appreciate the digitalisation of paper-based processes, especially one which would involve the use of snail mail, to a purely electronic one.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But for consequential documents, such as the Election Department (ELD)'s nomination papers or residential sale and purchase agreements, for example, there is a certain degree of comfort and confidence from the tactile experience of touching and signing a physical document.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The digital divide is thus real and cannot be ignored, as can be seen from recent experiences of residents choosing a physical TraceTogether Token instead of downloading the TraceTogether App, or the SingapoRediscovers Vouchers, on which many residents have shared with me feedback on the convoluted digital process of redeeming some of these vouchers.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As such, I would like to ask if the Ministry would consider retaining the option for donors to draft their LPA on a hard copy version of Form 1, if it is preferred, rather than only for exceptional circumstances?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I note that for CPF nominations, while this can be done online, there remains an option for members to complete a hard copy form to be submitted at the CPF Service Centres as well.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Further, it would also be preferable if multilingual support can be provided on the LPA Form itself, while also providing a guide in all four official languages to walk donors through the process of registering an LPA.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Looking through the guides provided by the OPG in its current website, I note that the LPA brochure, guides for caregivers, donees and deputies are all available in Chinese, Malay and Tamil as well.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But arguably the most important guide of all, the guide to the LPA is only available in English on the website.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I recognise that the Ministry will be assisting those less comfortable with digital services, by leveraging on community touchpoints such as the Citizen Connect Centres (CCCs) and the Integrated Public Service Centre (IPSC) at Our Tampines Hub.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Yet even at the CCCs, my understanding is that staff will be assisting residents with performing Government transactions online.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As it is an important document to make, elderly residents who may not be comfortable with digital forms, especially one in English and may not wish to complete the LPA form all at one go.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As friendly as the CCC staff may be, elderly residents may also wish to consult their children or other relatives whom they trust to get a second opinion on the LPA and a physical form would better facilitate this whole process.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The importance of having hard copies and multilingual support is thus even more important, given the demographic of LPA donors today.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I wonder, if the Ministry has conducted any study into why this is the case and whether efforts can also be made to encourage more men to make an LPA?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: (In Mandarin):   I believe that if one day we lose mental capacity due to ageing or other factors, we would hope that someone whom we trust, someone who is reliable and capable can handle our personal welfare and financial matters on our behalf.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: That being the case, it is extremely important to have a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) in advance to appoint someone whom we trust as our donee.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: When the amendment Bill is passed, Singaporeans will be able to apply for LPA online through the Office of the Public Guardian's online service and handle relevant transactions such as submitting online deputy’s report and making e-payments.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: However, for the elderly who are illiterate and do not know how to use computers, it will be more difficult for them to apply online.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The digitisation of LPA may also lead to concerns about electronic forms and public trust.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I understand from the MSF's announcement in May that Singaporeans who are not tech-savvy can go to Citizen Connect Centres located at CCs and the Integrated Public Service Centre at Our Tampines Hub for assistance.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: From 2014 to 2019, nearly 80% of donors are aged 50 and above and 55% are 60 years old and above, hence having a paper form LPA and multilingual support is all the more important.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I hope the Government can make more efforts to encourage more Singaporeans to have an LPA so that they are protected.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: There are three key steps under the existing process.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: First, the donor must choose someone he or she trusts to make decisions and decide on the decision powers to accord to the donee.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: If there is more than one donee, the donor must also decide whether the donees are to act jointly, or jointly and severally.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Second, the donor must attend before a Certificate Issuer, that is, a doctor, lawyer or psychiatrist, with the LPA, who will then sign and certify that the donor has mental capacity to make an LPA.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This is a crucial safeguard in ensuring that the donor is aware of the legal implications and has not been under duress or undue pressure in the creation of the LPA.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Third, the donor must submit the LPA and all relevant documents to the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) by post.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The OPG will then verify the documents and proceed to register the LPA if there are no valid objections.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We are living in an era where almost anything and everything is digitalised.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: It also means things are done even faster, smarter, easier and safer, especially with a low touch economy.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Accordingly, the proposed amendments which seek to establish an electronic transaction system for persons to create an LPA or carry out their transactions with the Office of Public Guardian digitally, is a timely and laudable move.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Even as the majority of Singapore rides the rapid waves of change in the digital sphere and we are moving forward in this space, I wish to highlight three concerns which I hope to see addressed we embark on this set of amendments.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: My wife and I did our LPA earlier this year and I must say the process is not a simple one.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: You need to read the fine print and there are quite a number of signatures and quite a number of documents and forms to go through.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: My first concern is with the seniors amongst us and whether the electronic process will be a boon or a bane to them as there are many who may not be electronically savvy and comfortable with the e-processes and may result in us losing out this group which are precisely the ones who need to make their LPAs most urgently, in case they lose their mental faculties with the passing of time and age.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The question we need to address is how the electronic process will help or encourage seniors to do up the LPA?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Will the system be multilingual as well and void of legalese?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I understand that the Office of Public Guardian has plans to work with the People's Association, the Infocomm Media Development Authority and other organisations to train and assist elderly persons.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This is a step in the right direction to evangelise the importance of the LPA.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: In addition, the Office of Public Guardian can also partner with NTUC and the Labour Movement as well as our union leaders to enhance the outreach to workers and union members.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: For a start, perhaps a special campaign can be embarked on to get all our union leaders to do up an LPA at a subsidised rate so that they can lead the way to encourage the workers and fellow members as they interact and engage them at the workplaces and the various shop floors.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Second is extending support at the local level and the needy.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Over in my Pioneer constituency, my community volunteer team and I had also organised and conducted a Facebook live webinar in October last year on "Wills, Estate Planning and Lasting Power of Attorney" to educate our residents on this very important topic.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We collaborated with Invictus Legacy centre to extend a very economical and affordable package to all Pioneer residents when they do up both an LPA and a simple Will, to the end of this year.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This was well-received by my residents and many of them shared that this was a useful and practical.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I recalled also doing a similar drive during my last term in Boon Lay constituency where we also extended a special package, but this time to the many needy and low-income residents there staying in rental flats.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: With this, I submit and suggest that OPG can work with the community and come up with a similar support scheme to assist low-income and needy residents to do up their LPAs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: There can also be proper benchmarks as now, there is a spectrum of charges imposed by Certificate Issuers depending on whether it is done through a lawyer, doctor or psychiatrist.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I am concerned for those who do not make their LPAs before losing mental capacity and their families and loved ones must now apply for deputyship with the Courts, which is a costly, time-consuming and cumbersome process, which quite a number of Members of this House have probably highlighted.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Would MSF be making any further changes to simplify the existing procedure, which would save time, costs and energy for all of us?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I note that there is a simplified application process for restricted use of monies of S$60,000 and below for certain categories of applications.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Does this disclosure obligation apply across the board?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Whilst in the process of improvement and advancement, it is important that we do not forget there are risks involved.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Hence, I seek clarity on the safeguards put in place and its adequacy as well as some clarifications regarding specific sections in the amendment Bill.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: First, ensuring robustness of the nomination process to prevent fraudulent nominations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Could the Ministry provide more specifics on the process and how in doing so, would prevent fraudulent nominations and avoid conflict of interest for donees with multiple appointments?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
