text: Further, how would the process account for and act as a preventive measure for those who are already experiencing an early onset of dementia or individuals with special needs?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Under section 10C(2), if more insights can be provided on what the Public Guardian foresees and hypotheses that could constitute valid reasons besides physical disability and electronic transaction system unavailability that is already outlined, for transactions that can be carried out in the form and need not be done electronically.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: If so, what would be the service level agreement in informing both the donor and the donee.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: This is a critical point as outlined in subsection (3) that and I quote, "when an error or omission has been corrected, the error or omission is treated as not having occurred".

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Should there be an error made by the Public Guardian in the course of rectification, what possible recourse can the donor or donee pursue?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Second, to ensure sufficient reach and provision of support for the move towards electronic LPA.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I think a few of my fellow colleagues have spoken about this.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: But I just want to emphasise on one point: with more elderly in Singapore living alone, are there any concrete plans to assist these seniors to file for LPA if they have not done so and to assign deputies earlier to them to better support them in their later years.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I believe, many of these seniors and special needs individuals may also be unfamiliar with the legal considerations, so how can we better serve their needs as we pivot towards electronic LPA.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: In clause 7, amendment of section 13(10), would steps be taken by the Public Guardian to authenticate the certificate from the registered medical practitioner, ensuring that it is a true copy?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Because as we go electronic and in many of these documentations, sometimes inevitably, that could be errors or that could be gaps.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: So, if we are not going to do this, how can the public agencies or organisations in which the donee is interacting on behalf of the donor, be assured that there is a validation process in place?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: On section 33A(3) and (4), could greater clarity be provided on the next step of action should the donor or donee raise objections to the proposed rectification or update of the register?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Last but not least, the cost that is involved and the transition process towards electronic LPAs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Because in clause 9, section 15A, it mentions that if there is any error to the non-electronic LPA, rectification can actually be made on the electronic version.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: So, my query is: what then would become of the non-electronic LPA?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Additionally, what is the transition process for the existing non-electronic LPA filed and the impact that it has on the existing protocols related to it?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: It will help with improving efficiency of processes for records checking and cross-usage amongst the authorities and I believe this is a very welcomed move.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: However, LPA is a sensitive document and it deals with the matters that affect the welfare of citizens, particularly more so for the vulnerable.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Thus, it is important that we maintain a robust system, albeit electronically, which manages the affairs with great accuracy and continues to uphold the trust between the institution and the public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A smooth transition to the new electronic transaction system for LPAs will simplify the process of making and accessing LPAs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, if not managed well, the transition can cause more errors and put users off the new electronic transaction system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A sizeable number of donors who interact with the system will be the elderly and vulnerable who may require more guidance in navigating the electronic system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This makes it all the more important to closely and carefully manage the transition.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have four points for clarification on this Bill on the transition process.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the rectification of relevant errors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 11(12)(B)(II) also addresses the situation where a PG decides not to rectify a relevant error.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify under what circumstances will the PG not rectify a relevant error?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, can the Parliamentary Secretary confirm that for the 90-day period before the electronic copy is treated as being free from error, the non-electronic copy remains the LPA?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary also then confirm that the donee and third parties are entitled to rely on the non-electronic copy in the 90-day period before the electronic copy becomes the LPA, even if there are discrepancies in the non-electronic copy, which the PG may decide not to rectify in the electronic copy?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on parties that have relied on relevant errors in carrying out transactions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Where a transaction is entered based on a relevant error, which is corrected, can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify the effect of the correction on the transaction?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Does the transaction remain valid or will the transaction be unwound?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask this because, according to section 10D(3), the error is treated as not having occurred, which may mean that the basis of the transaction no longer exists and should be unwound.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, section 16A(2) provides that a person is entitled to rely on the electronic copy with the relevant error in relation to the transaction, which suggests that the transaction remains valid.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify how this potential contradiction should be reconciled?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third point is on suspected fraud or undue pressure on a donor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the new section 31A(1), a donor may be interviewed if the PG has reasonable cause to suspect that fraud or undue pressure has been used to induce the donor to execute the instrument.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to interviewing the donor, does the PG have the power to interview persons related to the donor or to interview the donee?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the event that the PG is of the view that there is sufficient evidence to show that fraud or undue pressure was, in fact, used to induce the donor to execute the instrument, will the PG intervene, regardless of the donor's stated wishes?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What are the steps a PG will take in relation to a donee that it suspects is using fraud or undue pressure to influence multiple donors to appoint him or her as a donee?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My fourth point is on how the transition to the electronic transaction system will be implemented.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 10(C)(1) requires a person to use the electronic transaction system if they wish to register an instrument to create an LPA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 10(C)(2) contemplates that there may be some circumstances where a transaction cannot be carried out using the electronic transaction system due to a person's physical disability or other circumstances.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the	Parliamentary Secretary elaborate on the circumstances under which a person may be exempted from using the electronic transaction system?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The elderly and the vulnerable who may use and need the LPA most may also be the demographic that faces the most difficulties using this new electronic transaction system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that the Office of Public Guardian (OPG) has already shared its many initiatives and roadshows to educate and provide assistance for using the electronic transaction system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The UK has also implemented an online system for LPAs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The UK took a gradual rollout approach to their four million registered LPAs by opening up the system in batches to LPAs registered in different years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What are the lessons the Ministry has identified from the UK's rollout of their online system?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How have these lessons been incorporated into the Ministry's and OPG's efforts to ensure the rollout is a smooth one in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Mandarin):   To most Singaporeans, LPAs sound depressing and remote.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, there will come a day when you and I may be bedridden and have to rely on someone we trust to continue to live with dignity.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Since we have to appoint someone to handle our property and other important affairs through an LPA eventually, the LPA application process should be made easy.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Here, I would like to discuss the impact of LPA digitalisation on Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Public Service in Singapore has always been at the forefront of digitalisation.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: During the pandemic, digitalisation has helped our elderly to learn about and use email, internet banking and video conferencing.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, this does not mean that they do not fear digital services.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The key to make the leap across the digital divide is not knowledge but confidence.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How are we going to instill confidence in our elderly towards digitalisation?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Digital services will not completely replace customised services.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To many Singaporeans, convenience from digitalisation is merely a function which is a complement to face-to-face services.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In order to boost the confidence of the people, we need to make digital LPA easy to understand, use and trustworthy.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: At the same time, automated services should come with a human touch and be more personalised.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, the hallmark of a 21st century government is its ability to digitise its functions and processes and the Singapore Government has made leaps and bounds in this regard, such as the digitisation of citizen data on Singpass, payments on PayNow and even, to many of our citizens' delight, replacing parking coupons with an app.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, Mr Speaker, today, we are here to debate the digitisation of a service that is arguably of more concern to a thinner, more vulnerable slice of our society, such as the elderly as well as adults with special needs – the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These LPAs are not a matter that should be taken lightly.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While the prudent and forward-thinking make LPAs pre-emptively, many Singaporeans only consider LPAs as they get on with age out of the concern that, one day, they may not have the ability to make proper judgements over their own welfare, property and other personal affairs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Effectively, to make an LPA is to commit to let someone else decide what you should eat, where you should stay and how you should live should the fateful day come that you are not able to make these decisions yourself.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I recall someone I know in his early 50s asking me for help with the change of a file name on a document that is stored on his phone.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is unfamiliar terrain for many and then even for some.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Understandably then, the electronic LPA system, with implications reaching farther than WhatsApp video calls, may daunt many seniors who cannot find the confidence and assurance to traverse the digital divide.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: An online system is only as useful as those who are able to find it useful and set itself up to be an exhibit in the museum of digital assets if not well implemented.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that most of the online LPA system's intended audience will be daunted by fears associated with crossing the digital divide compounded by the pressure of making an LPA while they still can, we must stand ready to provide support for using these systems.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Crossing the digital divide is not just a matter of know-how but, in many cases, it is a matter of confidence.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Providing a personal touch, especially on something as personal and life-changing as LPAs, through social services or other equivalent means will give our residents the encouragement, assurance and motivation to set up LPAs over the well-meaning online system.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: On the extreme end, parents or relevant caregivers assume deputyship over these individuals, making decisions on their behalf in matters akin to an LPA.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, special needs and, indeed, mental incapacity, are a spectrum and we find a great diversity of conditions.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some cases are more visible than others while many other such conditions are virtually invisible to the untrained eye.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For example, should an individual who experiences episodes that result in delusions seek to make an LPA, how would the certificate issuer be able to ascertain that the basis on which the individual applies for an LPA is grounded in reality?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would an untrained personnel be able to make an assessment based on a one-off interaction with a special needs adult?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These are situations that are not easy, even with physical interactions and online submissions make it even more tricky.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The Mental Capacity Act has continuously updated itself over the years, strengthened its mechanisms to ensure that you, me, our friends and family will be taken care of with respect and dignity, held carefully in the cradle of trust.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: And this must be so throughout our lives.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: More so when we can no longer make decisions, either because of dementia or because of an accident or other illnesses.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As we move ahead with the roadmap to digitalise, we must ensure that we continue to build trust in the system as we embark on this journey.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: I applaud the effort for digital avenues for those who are less comfortable with digital services, to enable more to better understand its mechanisms and to embark on this transit.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: With the new electronic transaction system, some would have concerns with its security.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Through interactions with Yio Chu Kang residents, I have encountered problems due to an absence of LPA.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Most recently, a resident, Mr K, came to see me at a Meet-the-People session.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: His father suffered from advanced dementia and was in a nursing home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Mr K wanted to sell off his father's flat to pay for his father's nursing home charges.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: His father did not execute an LPA when he was mentally capable of doing so.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, Mr K was stuck in limbo.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To obtain legal permission, he would have to apply to the Courts to be appointed as a deputy.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have proposals in three broad areas to enhance the Bill further.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, we should make the process even more convenient for residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I noted that the requirement for the donor to appear before the LPA certificate issuer, or CI, is retained.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I understand the rationale, this safeguard of meeting in person still presents a challenge to donors who have mobility problems.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I hope that the Government can look out for this group of donors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Perhaps the Silver Generation Office can be roped in to do house visits.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They can help to make clarifications and arrange for a CI to certify the LPA in the comfort of seniors' homes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some medical practitioners and law firms already offer house visits.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: OPG should consider including those who provide such options on their websites and in the directory of CIs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should also consider having the process authenticated using digital fingerprints.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Banks and hospitals are already doing this for their forms and transactions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This will be useful for residents who may have suffered from a stroke and have difficulty signing physical documents, or those who are illiterate among our elderly.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Next, Mr Speaker, Sir, along with increased convenience, we need to make sure that there are sufficient safeguards in place.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With digitisation, a growing concern is the rising trend of data leaks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In this case, we are looking at potential leaks of highly personal information.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It could leave donors vulnerable to online fraud or blackmail.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Government safeguard our data in the event of a cybersecurity breach?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How can donors be assured that they will not be left to their own devices to navigate the associated issues?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Separately, there was public feedback for the OPG to assist healthcare professionals and providers to retrieve the LPA and donee's contact information in a timely and cost-efficient manner.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Currently, healthcare practitioners may login via Singpass to the OPG's e-services portal to make a search request.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The search results indicate whether the patient has made an LPA and the relevant details of the donee.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As the LPA will now be digital, can an LPA be automatically updated on the National Electronic Health Record system?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is so that in the event that an LPA needs to be activated, the healthcare professional need not wait two working days and pay $20 just to know who to contact.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I note that as part of the additional safeguards for donors, the Public Guardian may interview the donor.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Public Guardian may disclose to the donor the number of LPAs for which his or her prospective donee has already been appointed, or intends to be appointed.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is in the scenario if there is suspicion that fraud or undue pressure was used to induce a donor from making an LPA or appoint a particular person to be his or her donee.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Beyond this, another suggestion would be to make it mandatory for donees to notify the OPG of their intention to exercise their authority before doing so.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is to better protect donors from abuse.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Requiring the donee to notify the OPG can act as a road bump to make some potential abusers think twice.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Checks and processes could also be added to look into cases where a Singaporean with living blood-related family members decides to appoint an unrelated person as his donee.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: According to the recent population census, more people are choosing to remain single.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some married couples are opting to go childless.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, we will likely see more Singaporeans choosing unrelated donees due to the lack of younger relations to count on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The 2020 edition of LPA Form 1 requires the donor to specify the relationship of the donee to the donor.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This helps to alert the OPG should an unrelated donee be appointed.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Hence, OPG should institute precautions when such unrelated donees are appointed, especially when LPA applications involve vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, we should do more with regard to awareness and outreach to make sure more residents know about this important process.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I wish to circle back to a point I made when I spoke on the Electronics Transaction (Amendment) Bill earlier this year.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should review the fundamentals of the LPA application process to ensure that is user centric.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Although the LPA is for adults above the age of 21, statistically, elderly Singaporeans are more vulnerable to mental incapacitation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should, therefore, continue to focus our efforts on seniors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Advanced Care Planning, or ACP, is a critical component of ageing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The LPA may be important in ensuring that ACP is properly implemented in tandem.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should one have already made an LPA, it would be ideal and advisable for one's donee and the nominated healthcare spokesperson to be the same person.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is to avoid possible disagreements when making healthcare decisions on one's behalf.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I hope that the Government will look into incorporating ACP options into the LPA drafting process on the electronic system.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Both Ministries should also build an integrated process from the Social Service Agencies, or SSAs, to the healthcare institutions to encourage this effort.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: SSA officers should be trained to provide this service.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In the hospitals and polyclinics, they should actively highlight LPA and ACP matters to their patients.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: OPG should also have a central hotline to provide support for all the GPs and SSAs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: LPA consultations should be made more accessible in various languages and dialects.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, the new online LPA service should be made available in four languages.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Extending this further, we should take a whole-of-Government approach for outreach and awareness.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should start early because the risks of stroke and dementia are higher as we age.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Whilst moving towards making the LPA process through OPGO more convenient is in the right direction, we need to make sure safeguards are in place and encourage greater outreach and awareness.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This reassures donors that their interest will be taken care of should they lose their mental capacity one day.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, I support the Mental Capacity (Amendment) Bill to facilitate more Singaporeans to apply for an LPA.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although I agree that LPAs be done electronically, I am concerned that the seniors who are not tech-savvy will be discouraged to submit their applications.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although there are community touch points such as the Citizen Connect Centres (CCCs) and the Integrated Public Service Centre (IPSC) at Our Tampines Hub to provide assistance to seniors who are less comfortable with the use of digital services, I am still worried that not all seniors who are not tech-savvy will go to these places for help, especially those who are immobile.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Like my colleague Member of Parliament Mr Yip Hon Weng, I would like to suggest that MSF consider mobilising Silver Generation Ambassadors (SGAs) to promote and assist in the application of LPA.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: SGAs can do house visits, help to guide and assist seniors who are immobile in the application of LPA.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will benefit seniors who are not tech-savvy or immobile.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): It is encouraging for me to know that MSF would be expecting over 40,000 applications for Lasting Power of Attorney, or LPA for short, by the end of 2021.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This makes the latest amendments to the Mental Capacity Act a timely move.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given that one in 10 Singaporeans aged 60 and above have the chance of being diagnosed with dementia, and with the numbers expected to rise to 80,000 in 2030, I believe that the LPA should be widely promoted to all Singaporeans as it allows an individual to make an early, informed and personal choice of a proxy decision-maker or donees whom they can trust.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This reassures donors that their interest will be well taken care of should they lose their mental capacity one day.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The focus on my speech will be on the concerns and needs of seniors who are intending to apply for the LPA.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although MSF will be leveraging community touchpoints, such as the Citizen Connect Centres and the Integrated Public Service Centre at Our Tampines Hub, to provide assistance for seniors who are less comfortable with the use of digital services, there is a need to consider also seniors who have mobility issues and are not technologically comfortable.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: SGAs can help to guide and assist seniors who are immobile and cannot approach the Citizen Connect Centres by themselves in the application.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, special considerations can be made for seniors, who are immobile, to have the LPA Certificate Issuers (CIs) visit their homes together with the SGAs, to complete the LPA application, to give them the peace of mind.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am concerned that this may create an opportunity for vulnerable seniors to be targets of fraud by fraudulent donees who want to take advantage of them.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Without the requirement for donors and donees to meet up, seniors might be unknowingly coaxed into creating an LPA appointment by fraudulent donees.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although donors are still required to meet with the Certificate Issuers (CIs) to ensure that the donor has the mental capacity to make the LPA and understands the effect of an LPA, without a third person witnessing the donees' identity, it can become challenging for the Certificate Issuers to act as a safeguard in preventing fraud from occurring.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In recent times, there have been several noteworthy cybersecurity breaches on some cloud computing providers.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Should a security breach result in e-LPA documents being amended without the donors' or donees' knowledge, a transaction executed in good faith based on the LPA may result in a loss for the donors and/or liability for the donees.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How would the parties be protected, especially when the transaction relates to the donors' personal welfare, property and affairs?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Should the transaction that is in progress when the breach occurred be halted to determine if there has been any adversarial impact made to the LPA?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This would go some way to protect the interests of all parties.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These decisions can range from making simple bank transactions to applying for an HDB flat.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Therefore, it is important to appoint a reliable and trustworthy proxy decision-maker early, so that both the donor and their family members have peace of mind, knowing that their welfare and interests will be well taken care of when they become mentally incapacitated.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding the considerations raised, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree that there are many benefits to be gained from the digitalisation of the processes for the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In addition to greater convenience, the new system is more efficient and precious time can be saved with faster transactional time.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the OPGO system will be housed under the Government Commercial Cloud, I am sure that the system will be secured by the same standard of cybersecurity measures as for all other data and information held by the Government.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am glad to note that for those who are less digitally savvy, they will be able to arrange for personalised consultations by making appointment at the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) and seek help at Citizen Connect Centres located at community centres nationwide.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to ask the Ministry if the planned roadshows to boost public awareness of LPAs will be affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Is there any possibility of bundling workshops on LPAs with the Singapore Digital Office's courses to improve our elderly's digital literacy, thereby killing two birds with one stone?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For those with mobility problems and who do not know how to go online, will the Ministry assist them by sending a roving team to their homes to help them register LPAs, much like MOH roving vaccination team?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): Next, I would like to share my concerns about the additional safeguards for donors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am worried that such safeguards are not sufficient.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How can we ensure that elderly, in particular, those who are less educated, will not be cheated?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is particularly a concern where the donors and donees are not related.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Donees have control over the financial assets of the donor.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If they siphon away such resources for themselves, ultimately, the other family members or the Government will have to pick up the tab or pay for the care of the donors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With the increasing number of singles and our rapidly ageing population, the number of such vulnerable, and usually elderly, donors is likely to increase.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have already had cases of opportunistic donees in the past.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There is certainly no lack of predatory scammers looking to gain the trust of lonely elderly persons to take advantage of them.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I appeal to the Ministry to consider implementing additional measures to screen potential donees for the protection of donors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Medical diagnosis has to be submitted when applying for a Court order to appoint a pro bono donee, in order to help a client who has lost his or her mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Assuming the client has an existing medical record which states that he has lost his mental capacity and the record is stored in the National Electronic Healthcare Record.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This current process is time-consuming and does no service to the patient.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Notwithstanding the above-mentioned queries, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Because this Bill matters, and should matter, to each one of us.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The Mental Capacity Act has come a long way, since it was passed in Parliament in 2008 and came into effect in 2010.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In the last 10 odd years, attitudes and mindsets on mental capacity have shifted in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: More people are open to contemplating and planning for morbidity, and indeed, mortality.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In other words, planning for disease, dying and death.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Yet, it is estimated that one in 10 in Singapore aged 60 and above may get dementia.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In advanced stages of the disease, a patient will lose the ability to make decisions for him- or herself, on his or her personal welfare, property, money and other affairs.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And as our population ages, there will be more and more of such patients.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The key point is, it can happen to any senior.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: An unfortunate accident, for example, or a stroke, can rob a person of his or her ability to decide and act for him- or herself.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And, so, loss of mental capacity can really happen to any one of us.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Not a pleasant thought, but a necessary one.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And, so, this is why every one of us should think about and plan for the loss of our own mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And after 11 years of the Mental Capacity Act being in force, I believe it is time for the practice and the implementation of the Act to move into a new phase, shift to a higher gear, and gather even more momentum.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Therefore, the proposed amendments to this Act are very timely and I stand in full support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The move to make the LPA application and registration process electronic by default is a very significant move, a major shift from the practice today.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: No more wet ink signatures, no more multiple changing of hands of hard copy application forms.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The proposed move is also in line with our broader digital Government strategy, allowing for much more frictionless transactions between citizen and Government at different stages in life, and for different life cycle needs.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: There may be concerns that the shift to electronic LPA making could inadvertently exclude the very seniors for whom this move is intended to bring convenience to, because our seniors might not be digitally savvy.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: On this, I am confident that the Government has created sufficient touchpoints and resources in the community, to make sure that seniors who need help with electronic LPA making, in particular, and digital transactions with the Government in general, will get the help that they need.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In MSF’s public consultation exercise, I saw a suggestion to remove the need for in-person attendance before the Certificate Issuer (CI), in order to make the process even more convenient.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In other words, make the process completely electronic, just between man and the system.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The Bill has, however, retained the in-person attendance before a CI as a critical safeguard and I support this, as it would preserve confidence in the revamped process.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: But, more importantly, I think the feedback brings into focus a larger point that convenience needs to be seen against the other dimension of importance and I will explain this.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I know of seniors who have 10, 15, 20 appointments with doctors each year.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Almost all of these are attendances in person, although tele-consults are becoming more common.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And yet, seniors do not find these in-person attendances with doctors excessively inconvenient because, ultimately, these are about their health and health is, of course, important; and so it should be with LPAs.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The general point is this: while the Bill seeks to make the LPA-making process as convenient as possible, ultimately, our attitudes towards an LPA, the importance that we attach to an LPA, must really move to a higher plane.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: An LPA should be as important as good health, because having an LPA is part of planning well and living well.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And having an LPA is part of overall good health and well-being.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And so, just like good health, we need LPA adoption in Singapore to be much more widespread.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: How can we get many more to be aware of LPA, to be aware of mental capacity issues in the first instance, and how can we get many more to then recognise its due importance and actually take action to make an LPA?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: First, I would like to suggest that MSF partners with healthcare providers to open up a whole new frontier of LPA touchpoints in the community.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I believe that every patient passing through the doors of our polyclinics should be screened for LPA coverage, and for those that are not covered, the correct care planning conversations should take place in the polyclinic, there and then.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I believe the same screening should happen in our Specialist Outpatient Clinics and even the wards in public hospitals.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The screening should take place in our day care and senior activity centres across the island.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I think we ought to incorporate LPAs as part of standard health and care protocol for our seniors, going forward.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: And I hope that healthcare settings will get the right resources, for example, special LPA Ambassadors and/or training for existing staff, to carry out the right conversations.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Second, I suggest that we leverage the Silver Generation Office to promote LPAs door-to-door, engage and spread the message door-to-door, just like how we did for COVID-19 vaccination.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The need for inoculation against poor planning or no planning ought to be as important as the need for inoculation against disease.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Third, to better reach out to potential donees – youths, young adults, even middle-aged citizens – and encourage them to broach these conversations with their parents, grandparents, loved ones, we should utilise various channels, online and offline, again to reach out to these potential donees and get the message across.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Fourth and, finally, IMDA has been training thousands of seniors in a range of digital skills like Singpass, WhatsApp and e-payment, through the Seniors Go Digital programme.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I hope that MSF can work with IMDA to incorporate LPAs and make it a standard offering in the Seniors Go Digital Programme, going forward.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: To conclude, in fact, we need seniors to adopt not just LPA, but also Advance Care Planning (ACP), make a Will and make a CPF Nomination, as part of a comprehensive plan to live well and eventually leave well, for the benefit of themselves and their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Every senior – an LPA, an ACP, a Will, a CPF Nomination.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: That should be our overarching goal, to ensure that all bases are covered for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This Bill is the first of many steps that we would need to take in that direction.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: At the same time, the new process will not be at the expense of donor protection.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This approach is not only in line with the Government's vision of digital transformation in the public sector, but will also bring greater convenience to members of the public who are interested to be a donor or a donee.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Some people, especially the elderly, are worried that they do not know how to use computers or online platforms.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I am confident that the Government has provided sufficient service centres and resources within the community to help the public in need.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Notwithstanding the details of the amendment Bill, I feel that the fundamental significance of the Bill lies in wider public awareness of LPA and its importance.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In this respect, we still have a lot to do because too few Singaporeans have done an LPA.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The LPA allows us to designate a donee whom we trust to decide and execute matters pertaining to our welfare, property and finance on our behalf after we lose our mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: In other words, making an LPA is a precaution.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: If we lose mental capacity, the donee will become somebody we can fall back on. "If I were to lose mental capacity" may not be a phrase that sounds very pleasant, but it should still be addressed while we can.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: After all, the elderly in polyclinics, public hospitals or day centres should be screened to see if they have an LPA.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: If we notice that the elderly has no LPA, then the staff or volunteer should immediately have a conversation with the elderly and explain what an LPA is about.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Next, we should also tap on the Silver Generation Ambassadors and the Silver Generation Office (SGO) to do house visits just as how we promote the COVID-19 vaccination, because a comprehensive life plan is as important as vaccination.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: We should also make use of all the online and offline channels to encourage more young and middle-aged persons to discuss LPA matters with their parents, grandparents and loved ones.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Looking ahead, I hope that every senior citizen will not only have an LPA, but also have an Advance Care Plan, a Will as well as a CPF nomination.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I hope that we can move towards this goal step by step.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I will first like to declare that I am a practising lawyer and the co-chairperson of the Law Society's Pro Bono Services' Community Legal Clinic Committee.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For the past few years, as part of the effort to increase community law awareness, I have been going on radio talk shows on a monthly basis.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The topic mainly surrounds estate planning, in particular, the importance of Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And as part of our Woodgrove's GEL mission where L pertains to law awareness, out of the six law awareness talks organised for the past one year in Woodgrove, four sessions have been focused on sharing with our Woodgrove residents on the importance of estate planning.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many people often think that estate planning is something only wealthy individuals would consider doing.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In actual fact, it is equally important, if not more important, for people of lesser means in our society.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Take, for example, an elderly couple who only has each other to depend on, relying only on their retirement savings and their HDB asset.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What happens if the husband suddenly becomes comatose as a result of a severe stroke?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will the wife be able to sell or rent out their HDB flat in order to raise funds for payment of her husband's hefty medical expenses?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can she withdraw monies out from her husband's fixed deposit account to purchase necessary medical equipment required now by her bedridden husband?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While both options will allow her to manage her bedridden husband's personal welfare, property and affairs, the second one is often considered, as what my parliamentary colleague, Mr Patrick Tay, mentioned in his speech yesterday, a cumbersome and costly process, notwithstanding the fact that most Court applications for appointment of the deputy takes around three to four months to complete for a straightforward case.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As such, during my past 10 years of serving in the community, I have been a strong advocate of educating the public on the importance of doing an LPA, especially amongst our senior citizens.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In fact, during the Parliament Sitting in October last year, I had posed a question to MSF, enquiring whether the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) has plans to implement online registrations for LPAs.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Amidst this COVID-19 pandemic, we have begun to see more people, including lawyers, working from home.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Interviews with clients are conducted most of the time through virtual platforms.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This prevents the spread of the virus and enables those who are physically disabled and/or residing overseas to stay connected and run their errands without stepping out of the house.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It has always been my hope that through digitalisation, the process of registering an LPA will be simplified in the perspective of the donors and the donees, thereby encouraging more people, especially those with mobility issues, to sign up for one.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With that said, just like what several of my parliamentary colleagues who have spoken before me have raised, I likewise envisage that there will be two issues that may occur when we move the registration of LPA onto an electronic transaction system.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As mentioned by Mayor Denise Phua and Mr Louis Ng yesterday, as well as Ms Ng Ling Ling a moment ago, I concur that the elderly and the vulnerable groups in our community will require more assistance to access the Internet and navigate the online system.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I wish to elaborate on this issue in Mandarin please, Mr Speaker.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In Mandarin):   After the Mental Capacity (Amendment) Bill is passed, Singaporeans will be able to register an LPA online through the new online service offered by the Office of the Public Guardian.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To encourage more people to do an LPA while they are mentally sound, besides making the application process faster and more convenient, I think we must first ensure that both the donor and the donee, who is required to provide his or her consent, are able to access the internet and log into the relevant portal easily, especially those who may not be digitally savvy.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As they would often bring along their tablets while doing their rounds, they would be well-suited to provide assistance in terms of internet access, especially for those with mobility issues.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In English): The second issue pertains to whether one knows how to fill up the e-form and understand the legal consequences of each option selected.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, when the donor selects the option to empower the donee to give or refuse consent to start or continue with healthcare and medical treatments, are they both aware that such empowerment does not mean that the donee will be able to make a decision on whether to provide extraordinary life sustaining treatment to prolong the donor's life?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This can only be done if the donor signs a separate legal instrument called the Advance Medical Directive (AMD) and many people often misunderstood the meaning behind this.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While I note that the staff at these community touchpoints will be trained to help those who have difficulties using the OPG portal to make their LPA electronically, it is my humble opinion that the services to be provided should only pertain to assisting them with the technical issues on assessing the portal.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, how to log on and sign electronically.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The LPA is, after all, a legal instrument and it is best that the donor and donee understand the legal consequences before signing their names.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, I propose that the portal should have a feature where a virtual meeting can be conducted, where the donor, donee and Certificate Issuer log in at the same time.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Certificate Issuer will take parties through the e-form and ensure that both the donor and donee understand the content and e-sign at the same instance.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: During the course of the meeting, the Certificate Issuer should also be using a standard due diligence framework checklist that is to be created by the OPG, to ascertain whether parties have the mental capacity to execute such a legal instrument.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Lastly, this virtual meeting should be recorded and stored in the portal database.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These recorded footage may come in useful when the Public Guardian is ascertaining, subsequently, whether the donor had previously been induced into executing the LPA.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As mentioned earlier, an LPA is just one component of estate planning.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: During the Budget debate earlier this year, I suggested that we consider setting up an estate planning portal online with support from multiple Ministries to start educating households on the essential legal knowledge and encourage them to begin estate planning for contingencies.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This portal will be dedicated to administrative matters, such as CPF nominations, lodging of LPA applications, AMDs, as well as the registering of Wills.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One can even consider setting out their funeral arrangement plans through this portal.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Upon the passing of a loved one, the next of kin can assist to notify through this portal and extract the necessary information required to kickstart the administration of the estate.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This portal can also provide further value by collaborating with the Law Society, which can assist to devise a way for the platform to dispense legal advice virtually.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I was heartened to learn that as part of the LifeSG initiative and to encourage more people to begin their end-of-life planning comprehensively, MOH, Public Service Division and the Smart Nation and Digital Government Group have launched the My Legacy portal last year.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I trust that OPG is in touch and in the midst of collaborating with the abovementioned agencies to ensure that the registration of LPA through My Legacy portal will be seamless and I am hopeful that the portal incorporates the features which I have recommended above.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Lastly, I wish to seek clarification on the cost of registering the LPA.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I believe this would further motivate fellow Singaporeans to apply and subscribe to LPA Form 1 soon.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, digital systems, records and transactions have vulnerabilities as they require electricity and Internet access.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am worried about eventualities such as power outages, system malfunctions and cyberattacks.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry share in greater detail what measures are in place to mitigate such risks and what back-up plans are in place?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Do we have foolproof back-up for all information in the databases?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The other issue is the possibility of disputes when LPAs have been changed, particularly just before the donors lose their mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In some cases, relationships among donors, donees and family members may be complicated and even acrimonious.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is there any simplified processes in place to bring about expeditious resolution for such cases?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can some sort of insurance be arranged to protect donors?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the other hand, donees also face risks of legal suits and, hence, can they protect themselves with a form of professional indemnity insurance?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: An electronic transaction system will allow for faster and more secure registration for donors' benefit.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will also reduce the possibility of errors.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, I would like to introduce several proposals, to further safeguard the interests of all parties involved and, at the same time, to protect the reputation and integrity of the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) and Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) system.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am speaking from my own experiences as a pro bono lawyer helping laypersons make and file their LPAs.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Currently, donees make an online declaration not equivalent to a Statutory Declaration, before submitting information to third parties.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Bodies like the Association of Banks Singapore and Council for Estate Agencies already require donees to first produce medical reports, which show that the donor has lost his or her mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is a requirement before he or she can exercise the powers under the LPA.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Perhaps, it is useful to have such a general requirement and to make it mandatory for banks and real estate firms, who handle LPA-related transactions, to keep OPG or their regulators informed once a request to exercise LPA is made by a donee.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree with MSF's retention of requirement for a donor to visit the LPA Certificate Issuer (CI) in person because this will ensure the donor understands the scope and purpose of the LPA.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, I think it is equally important that the CI meets the donee as well.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, by having the CI meet the donee, this will also help the CI to flag to OPG if the donee already is a donee on other LPAs.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree with and understand MSF's reasoning to protect confidentiality and only disclose the number of LPAs on which the donee has been appointed, and that the choice is, ultimately, up to the donor.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, the capability and adequacy of the donee in exercising such powers may be limited if he or she is to administer various matters on behalf of several donors who have lost their mental capacity at the same time.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Surely, there is a limit to human abilities and dedication of time.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It would, thus, be useful to consider a requirement for the CI to highlight to OPG when facing donees who are multiple donees.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: OPG can then subsequently follow up and advise the donor that the chosen donee is a multiple donee, and if they want, they can make his or her informed choice.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Another aspect to look out for is the relationship between the donor and the donee or the lack of one.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Having donees who are non-family members, or who are no longer directly related by virtue of a divorce or a re-marriage, may give rise to potential misunderstandings or conflicts in the future.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this regard, it would be useful to consider requiring CIs to meet potential donees in person too and not just the donors.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Not only can the CIs ascertain the mental capacity of the donees but they can also raise the red flag to OPG if the donee to be appointed is a non-family member or if there is anything amiss.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It would also be useful if OPG is updated when there has been a change in the relationship between the donor and the donee.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Once we reach the age of 21, anyone of us can become a donor and appoint one or more persons whom we trust to become a donee to make decisions on our behalf in the unfortunate event that we lose our mental faculties.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: According to data from the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG), the number of LPAs registered has been on an upward trend.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The proposed amendments in the Bill are, therefore, timely as an online system will allow the Ministry to cater to a higher volume of LPA applications.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While it is encouraging to seeing an increasing number of LPA applications in recent years, we need to be aware that those who have registered as a doner remains a very small minority in our society and more must be done to address the stigma that comes associated with conversations about LPA.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is common to hear our loved ones, especially our parents and grandparents, dismiss discussions about registering an LPA with words like "touch wood", or more colloquially, "choy!" and, unfortunately, the conversation does not progress past this stage.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Amongst the young, many simply think that this is something for our seniors to do.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can the Ministry provide a demographic breakdown of applicants that have become donors in the past five years and share its plans to destigmatise the topic of LPA and encourage adoption especially among our seniors?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How would someone know that someone else has impersonated them either as a donor or a donee?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How will OPG know if fraud or undue pressure was used to induce a donor to make an LPA or appoint a particular person to be their donee?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I would also like to ask if there had been instances of a donee being appointed by multiple donors and whether this would be a key factor in determining fraudulent digital LPA applications.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Lastly, I would like to echo what several Members have raised yesterday and today, about the importance of ensuring that digital LPA applications remain accessible to the less tech-savvy, particularly our seniors.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While I am glad to hear that MSF plans to leverage community touchpoints like the Citizen Connect Centres at our Community Centres, to aid those who need help, I believe that more can be done to assist our seniors at the hubs that they frequent.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Members' comments fall into five broad themes, namely: (a) support for those who need help navigating online services; (b) clarifications regarding the electronic transaction system OPGO; (c) cybersecurity; (d) protection of donors, donees and third parties; and (e) future developments in the mental capacity landscape.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many Members, such as Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Denise Phua, Mr Don Wee, Ms Hany Soh, Mr Leon Perera, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Melvin Yong, Ms Ng Ling Ling, Mr Seah Kian Peng, Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Yip Hon Weng have raised concerns about supporting those who need help navigating digital services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the support of many community partners, we will endeavour to leave no one behind in this digitalisation journey.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For the elderly with family, we encourage their family members to assist them and leverage Singpass' multi-user SMS Two-Factor Authentication (2FA).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Louis Chua would also be pleased to know that instructions on making the LPA in OPGO will be made available in the vernacular languages.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Further, the Office of the Public Guardian, or OPG, will train Certificate Issuers to navigate LPA applications on OPGO so that they, too, may support their clients.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also offer one-on-one consultation at OPG's physical office.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Hany Soh, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Xie Yao Quan would be glad to know that OPG is working with Silver Generation Ambassadors to connect seniors keen to make their LPAs, especially those living alone, with their nearest community touchpoints.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Citizen Connect Centres and Public Service Centre staff will be trained to help seniors make their LPAs or access LPA-related transactions online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Soh may be assured that the staff will not be advising on the appointments or the powers to be granted.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As for Mr Melvin Yong's suggestion to leverage Senior Activity Centres and regional social service agencies, OPG will work with them to direct their clients to the nearest touchpoint.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I also thank Mr Seah Kian Peng and Mr Patrick Tay for their suggestions on other potential partnerships to ensure accessibility.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For donors with mobility issues, such as physical disability or incarceration, LPA Certificate Issuers may visit them to certify their LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG representatives can also assist the physically disabled with their LPA applications at their homes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For the visually impaired, OPGO will include text-to-speech functions to guide them in completing their LPAs online.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Digital fingerprints, as suggested by Mr Yip Hon Weng, however, may not be necessary as we have replaced wet ink signatures with digital ones.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A parallel hard copy system for the majority, as suggested by Ms Denise Phua and Mr Louis Chua, would not be necessary but, as mentioned in my opening speech, we will allow hard copy submissions under exceptional circumstances.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Next, let me address some queries regarding OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan noted that errors in hard copy LPAs would be rectified on the electronic copy under clause 9 of the Bill and asked whether these hard copy LPAs containing errors would be superseded by the electronic copies on OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I note Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Louis Ng's concern on whether transactions may rely on hard copy LPAs containing errors and would like to assure that these errors, such as repeated page numbers, are highly unlikely.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG has checked through all scanned copies of existing registered LPAs to minimise any risk of errors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Therefore, while donees and third parties are not prevented from referencing the hard copy LPAs, the superseded hard copy LPA should not be relied upon for transactions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is because any note on the occurrence of certain important events will only be attached to the electronic LPA henceforth.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Such events include the donee's bankruptcy, which would revoke his power to manage the donor's financial matters.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As such, I strongly encourage all parties to rely on the electronic copy when transacting.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if the hard copy version of the LPA is the LPA during the 90-day period.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about the circumstances under which the Public Guardian will not rectify a notified error in the electronic copy of the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under the new section 11(14) of the MCA, which is inserted by clause 4 of the Bill, a "relevant error" refers to any disparity or inconsistency between the electronic copy and the LPA that has been registered.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Guardian will rectify every such error brought to her attention.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To his question on whether transactions relying on an electronic copy containing a relevant error would still be valid, the answer is yes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The new section 10D is not intended to cover rectification of any relevant error arising from the process of converting hard copy LPAs to electronic copies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng proposed to require express verification from the donors and donees before the electronic copy is treated as the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have made a considered decision not to do so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Donees and third parties will also be protected if they had respectively acted in reliance on the electronic copy or had transacted in good faith without knowing of the relevant error.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We do not wish to inconvenience most donors and donees to cater for an unlikely scenario.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan made a few technical queries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, on considerations for disclosing non-confidential information – this may be disclosed to Public Sector agencies or the public at large for reasons of public education or interest, for example, to correct any falsehoods regarding LPA statistics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Others seeking access would need the Public Guardian's approval to search the LPA register.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As rectifications would be based on information obtained from other Singapore Public Sector agencies, objections would be unlikely.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if MSF has incorporated lessons from the United Kingdom's online system for LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I wish to clarify that the UK's service does not allow for the online registration of electronic LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The LPA must still be printed and signed using wet ink signatures before submitting it to the UK OPG.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: What the UK's online service allows is the conversion of the hard copy registered LPAs into online summaries of the LPAs that can be shared with transacting parties.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In contrast, OPGO digitalises the entire LPA process, including the online creation of digitally-signed LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Given this, comparisons between OPGO and the UK's online system might not be apt but I take Mr Louis Ng's point on the need to ensure that the roll-out is smooth.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have conducted extensive stakeholder engagements and will involve them in User Acceptance Tests.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG will also be training Certificate Issuers on the use of OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Cybersecurity risks are not new but they are especially pertinent in light of important documents like the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPGO will be housed under the Government Commercial Cloud.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Cybersecurity measures will be in place to protect against hacking and data compromise.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For example, Personal Identifiable Information will be encrypted.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To address unscheduled system outage, OPGO data would be backed up daily across multiple geographical locations or zones in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Users will be informed of the disruption and may contact OPG's hotline for help.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Guardian will also check through all the LPAs submitted during the period of malfunction.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Should there be any issues, Miss Cheryl Chan may be assured that the Public Guardian will rectify it as soon as possible and notify the donors and donees affected within seven days of its rectification.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As these issues are likely to be easily rectified – for example, a person's NRIC being keyed in twice – donors and donees need not be too alarmed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If a donor or donee spots any discrepancies in the electronic LPA after OPGO has been restored, he or she can contact the Public Guardian to rectify it.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
