text: We will work closely across the Government as we develop the system and the specific protection clauses required.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I wish to reassure Members that we have taken steps to prevent unauthorised access and distribution of the electronic LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The electronic LPA will only be accessible to the donors and donees after they log on to OPGO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Donors or donees may share the LPA with third parties by making the request in OPGO and providing the email address of the transacting party to receive the electronic LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG will send a password-protected LPA to the transacting party.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Only parties authorised by the donors or donees may view the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Stringent security measures also prevent changes to the contents of the electronic LPAs without the donor or donee's knowledge when the document is signed with Singpass.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If the LPA is compromised, the changes will be detected and the digital signature will be reflected as invalid, thereby disabling it from being used.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many Members have made suggestions for further safeguards to protect donors, donees and third parties.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked for MSF to reconsider the removal of a witness for the donees’ signature.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have assessed that the risks of doing so are very low.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, the donee must log on to OPGO using Singpass 2FA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With 2FA, the donee must first enter his Singpass ID and password and, thereafter, enter a One-Time Pin (OTP) sent via SMS or use Face Verification.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Alternatively, the donee may log on to OPGO using the Singpass application.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These provide an additional security layer to prove the donee’s identity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, OPGO will send notifications to a donee at various points while the LPA is being created.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As the donee is kept informed in real time, he or she can alert OPG if someone is impersonating him or her.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, Ms Hany Soh, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Seah Kian Peng and Ms Yeo Wan Ling may be assured that even as we go digital, we have retained the most important safeguard for donors to execute the LPA in the presence of the Certificate Issuer.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This ensures that the donor has the mental capacity to make his or her LPA, including that the donee appointed is the person intended by the donor.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The class of professionals who may be Certificate Issuers are scoped to those whom we are confident possess the qualifications to certify that the donor understands the purpose and scope of the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim also asked to consider at least one meeting between donors, donees and Certificate Issuers or between Certificate Issuer and donees.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I seek Members’ understanding that we are aiming to strike a right balance between safeguards and convenience.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There is, currently, no requirement for donees to be present when the donor visits the Certificate Issuer.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It may be difficult for donors and donees to arrange a common time and space, given our work and family commitments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is especially so if the donees are overseas at the time of the donor’s execution of the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We wish to retain this convenience so that the LPA-making process is as accessible as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Furthermore, the donor should choose a person he trusts to make decisions on his or her behalf.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Should there be any doubts on the donee’s mental capacity, the donor would not have appointed him or her.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If more than one donee is appointed, any other concerned donee may also object to the registration of the LPA during the mandatory three-week waiting period.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked to consider additional protection measures before a donee may use the LPA to transact.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan had suggested for the Public Guardian to authenticate the medical report so that transacting parties are assured of its validity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Leon Perera and Mr Yip Hon Weng proposed that all donees should notify OPG of their intention to exercise their authority, especially for major decisions, before doing so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, the MCA already allows a third party to require a donee to produce a certificate from a registered medical practitioner, stating that the donor’s lack of capacity is likely to be permanent, for matters involving a donor’s property.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Transacting parties may refuse to accept the donee’s authority if the donee does not comply.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am not inclined towards a Statutory Declaration as this requires donees to seek a Commissioner for Oaths, which incurs more costs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We must not unnecessarily penalise the majority of cases that do not involve fraud.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG will also continue to remind stakeholders to conduct their due diligence checks and verify that the maker of the medical report is a doctor with a valid licence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Shawn Huang, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the amendment to allow the Public Guardian to disclose to the donor certain information concerning the donees.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They wish to clarify the process and how OPG could detect such occurrences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Guardian will assess the flagged case and interview the donor, if necessary.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Potential red flags, as Mr Don Wee noted, may include cases where the donee is unrelated to any of the donors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Guardian may also receive whistle-blowing complaints on the proposed donee.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Louis Ng raised an important point on whether the Public Guardian would intervene, regardless of the donor’s stated wishes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A key principle in the MCA is to respect the decision of a person with mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We must respect the donor’s wishes should he or she knowingly appoints a donee with multiple doneeships or declines to attend an interview with the Public Guardian, a possible scenario that Ms Sylvia Lim raised.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For Mr Melvin Yong’s and Ms Sylvia Lim’s information, the Public Guardian would interview the donor to assess if the donor had voluntarily made the LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If necessary, the Public Guardian may rely on her existing powers to obtain further information to determine the issue.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This approach would similarly be taken for cases that Miss Cheryl Chan has raised, for example, when the donor is already experiencing an early onset of dementia.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if the Public Guardian could interview persons other than the donor.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Guardian may exercise her investigative powers under the existing section 32 of the MCA to interview any person who has the relevant information relating to a donor who has lost mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As the number of doneeship appointments is confidential, we need to be careful on how much is shared and with whom.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Thus, under the new section 31A of the MCA, we have enabled the Public Guardian to disclose this information to the donor only so that he or she may make an informed decision.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Don Wee suggested additional measures to screen potential donees.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For example, Mr Seah Kian Peng asked to require the Public Guardian to disclose multiple doneeships in all cases.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I wish to clarify that the intent of the amendment is to cover select cases where there are reasonable grounds to doubt the integrity of the LPA-making process.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, a daughter may be appointed as donee for her father, mother and husband.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Certificate Issuer will also have certified that the donor is not under undue pressure or fraud to appoint a particular person as donee.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Guardian will exercise her discretion judiciously when disclosing the donees’ information in the exceptional cases where fraud or undue pressure is suspected.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Murali Pillai also proposed that the Public Guardian be allowed to disclose other relevant information which is material to the donor’s decision when appointing the donee, for example, if the donee has prior criminal convictions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if there is any recourse for mismanagement or breach of trust committed by the donee which does not require going to the Court.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Application to the Court is necessary as the Court plays the role as the finder of facts to determine whether mismanagement or breach of trust has occurred.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That said, the concerned party need only report the case to the Public Guardian.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Public Guardian can then take the case to Court, if necessary.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On Mr Gan’s suggestion to explore insurance for donors and donees to protect against the risk of legal suits, we will take this feedback onboard but we are mindful that this may incur higher costs for both donors and donees.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also raised another query regarding simplified dispute resolution options for disputing donors, donees and family members.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Sometimes, despite the best of intentions, conflicts may arise because of a communication breakdown or misunderstanding.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It may not be easy but I would encourage all disputing parties to talk through their differences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG may also refer these cases to mediation, family conferencing or counselling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked what might constitute "good reasons" where remote witnessing may be required.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These include cases where the person has contracted a highly contagious disease such that a Certificate Issuer may not visit in person.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under such exceptional circumstances, prior application by the donor is needed for the Public Guardian to assess the merits of the case and to ensure sufficient safeguards are in place for remote witnessing.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG will seek inputs from the various stakeholders on the safeguards and ensure that all the operational details are worked through before we implement this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Don Wee asked if there are plans to further simplify and expedite the deputyship process.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But I agree that more can be done.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We note the Members’ suggestions and will continue to explore ways to improve the process.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Xie Yao Quan emphasised the importance of a holistic pre-planning package.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: My Ministry has been working closely with MOH to encourage citizens to pre-plan and to make their LPAs and Advance Care Plans together.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Advance Care Plan allows a person to consider their care preferences and communicate their wishes to their "healthcare spokesperson", who can speak on their behalf in the future.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ideally, the donee will take on the role of the healthcare spokesperson so that he or she may not only communicate but also make the decisions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Hany Soh and Mr Yip Hon Weng would be pleased to know that the My Legacy portal already has an LPA-ACP tool which guides users to complete both forms.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are working with the My Legacy team to allow for system interfaces between OPGO and My Legacy, such that online LPA applications can be made on My Legacy, too.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will enable Singaporeans to consider making an LPA as they plan for other end-of-life matters.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPGO will also encourage donors to nominate their donees as their "healthcare spokespersons".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I also thank Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Yip Hon Weng for their suggestions to integrate the LPA into relevant healthcare protocols and Government processes, such as CPF nomination reviews.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the same spirit, Ms Denise Phua had asked if the Certificate Issuer pool could be expanded to other professionals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPGO will also include a search function enabling donors to locate the Certificate Issuers by location.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if the electronic LPAs would be automatically updated on the National Electronic Health Records system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are working to automatically approve search requests submitted in OPGO by pre-approved agencies, such as hospitals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will ensure healthcare professionals and providers can retrieve search results in a timely and cost-efficient manner.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Hany Soh and Mr Patrick Tay have raised some concerns on the costs of making an LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I, therefore, urge all Singaporeans to take advantage of the waiver and OPGO to make your LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, regarding Ms Soh’s query on whether we will waive the fees permanently, we will review this and share more when we are ready.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, Mr Patrick Tay asked if the Certificate Issuer fees may be waived, subsidised or benchmarked.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: OPG does not prescribe the fees charged as LPA certification is a professional service.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, the top 10 most visited Certificate Issuers are published on OPG’s website.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For those needing financial assistance, the OPG website lists not-for-profit providers offering subsidised LPA certification services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They include Life Point's LPA One-Stop Services, Potter's Place Community Services Society and Mount Alvernia Outreach Medical Clinic @ Enabling Village.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I fully agree with Ms Denise Phua, Mr Don Wee, Mr Louis Chua, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Seah Kian Peng and Mr Xie Yao Quan's call for more Singaporeans to make their LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In my opening speech, I have outlined how digitalisation would ease this LPA-making process.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua would be pleased to learn that MSF has been working closely with other Ministries and community partners to raise awareness on pre-planning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As mentioned, we work with the Silver Generation Ambassadors to reach out to seniors and their care-givers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While we have halted temporarily our physical roadshows due to the pandemic, OPG has continued to engage hospitals, banks, Senior Activity Centres and so on, to conduct virtual talks on LPA for their staff and clients.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But we can do more to widen our outreach in a sustained manner.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There are plans for a pre-planning campaign which will leverage digital and ground channels to reach out to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am also heartened by Mr Patrick Tay's sharing about the live webinar and economical pre-planning packages he had embarked on for his Pioneer constituency and hope that other Members would consider similar efforts in their constituencies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am glad that Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Seah Kian Peng had pointed out the taboo amongst seniors regarding LPAs and the misconceptions that some younger Singaporeans hold about pre-planning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I understand that the conversation about losing mental capacity can be difficult to broach.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But it is better to be prepared than to leave matters unclear for our families should we lose mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Fortunately, more young Singaporeans are grasping the importance of pre-planning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The full breakdown of the donors and donees by age is available on OPG's website.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to educate Singaporeans and stakeholders to address these misconceptions and promote pre-planning before considering more drastic measures like default LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked if there is an aspirational target for the number of LPAs that we want to achieve.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The truth is that the LPA take-up rate has been rising quite rapidly.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: My point is that we are moving in the right direction.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, targets aside, what we ought to do is to facilitate the LPA-making process and the launch of OPGO is yet another step to this end.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The current MCA also requires donees to take all practicable steps to help the donor to make a decision before treating him as being unable to do so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Family members who are the vast majority of donees are also well-placed to support their donors in making their decisions as much as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For unrelated professional donors, they are required to draft a care plan and check in regularly with the donor to ensure that their wishes are respected to the fullest extent.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Citizens and third parties alike will also have more confidence in transacting with the most up-to-date electronic LPAs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Digitalisation of the LPA and other transactions with the Office of the Public Guardian is especially timely, given the pandemic, which limits face-to-face interactions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The LPA is an important pre-planning tool in ensuring peace of mind not only for ourselves but also for our family members and loved ones as they will know our wishes and can carry them out if we were to lose mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With that, I thank all Members for your valuable inputs and support of this Bill.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I do not believe there are any clarifications because the Parliamentary Secretary has been very diligent in answering all the questions.      .
